entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6746"/><div sID="gen10341" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6746"/>13-15. The faith induced by God's display of power in their behalf was short lived, and their new rebellion and temptation was visited by God with fresh punishment, inflicted by leaving them to the result of their own gratified appetites, and sending on them spiritual poverty (<reference osisRef="Num.11.18">Nu 11:18</reference>).<div eID="gen10341" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10342" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">They soon forgat--</hi>literally, "They hasted, they forgat" (compare <reference osisRef="Exod.32.8">Ex 32:8</reference>). "They have turned aside quickly (or, hastily) out of the way." The haste of our desires is such that we can scarcely allow God one day. Unless He immediately answers our call, instantly then arise impatience, and at length despair.<div eID="gen10342" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10343" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">his works--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Deut.11.3">De 11:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.11.4">4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.9.14">Da 9:14</reference>).<div eID="gen10343" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10344" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">his counsel--</hi>They waited not for the development of God's counsel, or plan for their deliverance, at His own time, and in His own way. <div eID="gen10344" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6751"/><div sID="gen10351" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6751"/>19-23. From indirect setting God at naught, they pass to direct.<div eID="gen10351" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10352" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">made--</hi>though prohibited in <reference osisRef="Exod.20.4">Ex 20:4</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.20.5">5</reference> to make a likeness, even of the true God.<div eID="gen10352" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10353" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">calf--</hi>called so in contempt. They would have made an ox or bull, but their idol turned out but a calf; an imitation of the divine symbols, the cherubim; or of the sacred bull of Egyptian idolatry. The idolatry was more sinful in view of their recent experience of God's power in Egypt and His wonders at Sinai (<reference osisRef="Exod.32.1-Exod.32.6">Ex 32:1-6</reference>). Though intending to worship Jehovah under the symbol of the calf, yet as this was incompatible with His nature (<reference osisRef="Deut.4.15-Deut.4.17">De 4:15-17</reference>), they in reality gave up Him, and so were given up by Him. Instead of the Lord of heaven, they had as their glory the image of an ox that does nothing but eat grass. <div eID="gen10353" type="x-p"/>

Instead of the Lord of heaven, they had as their glory the image of an ox that does nothing but eat grass.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6753"/><div sID="gen10359" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6753"/>24-27. The sin of refusing to invade Canaan, "the pleasant land" (<reference osisRef="Jer.3.19">Jr 3:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.20.6">Eze 20:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.8.9">Da 8:9</reference>), "the land of beauty," was punished by the destruction of that generation (<reference osisRef="Num.14.28">Nu 14:28</reference>), and the threat of dispersion (<reference osisRef="Deut.4.25">De 4:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.28.32">28:32</reference>) afterwards made to their posterity, and fulfilled in the great calamities now bewailed, may have also been then added.<div eID="gen10359" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10360" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">despised--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Num.14.31">Nu 14:31</reference>).<div eID="gen10360" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10361" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">believed not his word--</hi>by which He promised He would give them the land; but rather the word of the faithless spies (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.78.22">Psa 78:22</reference>). <div eID="gen10361" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 24-27. The sin of refusing to invade Canaan, "the pleasant land" ( Jr 3:19 ; Eze 20:6 ; Da 8:9 ), "the land of beauty," was punished by the destruction of that generation ( Nu 14:28 ), and the threat of dispersion ( De 4:25 ; 28:32 ) afterwards made to their posterity, and fulfilled in the great calamities now bewailed, may have also been then added. despised-- ( Nu 14:31 ). believed not his word-- by which He promised He would give them the land; but rather the word of the faithless spies (compare Psa 78:22 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6759"/><div sID="gen10371" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6759"/><hi type="bold">31. counted ... righteousness--</hi>"a just and rewardable action."<div eID="gen10371" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10372" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for--</hi>or, "unto," to the procuring of righteousness, as in <reference osisRef="Rom.4.2">Ro 4:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rom.10.4">10:4</reference>. Here it was a particular act, not faith, nor its object Christ; and what was procured was not justifying righteousness, or what was to be rewarded with eternal life; for no one act of man's can be taken for complete obedience. But it was that which God approved and rewarded with a perpetual priesthood to him and his descendants (<reference osisRef="Num.25.13">Nu 25:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Chr.6.4">1Ch 6:4</reference>, &c.). <div eID="gen10372" type="x-p"/>

But it was that which God approved and rewarded with a perpetual priesthood to him and his descendants ( Nu 25:13 ; 1Ch 6:4 , &c.).

navigation_sections.title: Psa 106:1-48 . This Psalm gives a detailed confession of the sins of Israel in all periods of their history, with special reference to the terms of the covenant as intimated ( Psa 105:45 ). It is introduced by praise to God for the wonders of His mercy, and concluded by a supplication for His favor to His afflicted people, and a doxology.
